title: BCCI Overhauls Fitness Testing After India's Injury Crisis During England Tour
excerpt: The Board of Control for Cricket in India tightens Bronco Test and 2K run benchmarks at its Centre of Excellence after a wave of injuries derailed the 2026 white-ball tours.
body:
• The BCCI has tightened the Bronco Test cutoff from six minutes to 5 minutes 15–20 seconds, and introduced a mandatory back-to-back 2K run to be completed within 9–10 minutes.
  • The overhaul follows India's disastrous white-ball tours of Ireland and England, where multiple players including Jasprit Bumrah, Harshit Rana, and Nitish Kumar Reddy suffered injuries.
  • Top contracted players including Ravindra Jadeja, Rishabh Pant, and Yashasvi Jaiswal underwent mandatory pre-season fitness evaluations at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru.
  • A BCCI source revealed that some senior players had been given softer fitness targets, and pacer Harshit Rana was cleared for the UK tour while 4 kg overweight.

Stricter Benchmarks Replace Lax Standards

The BCCI's Centre of Excellence (CoE) in Bengaluru has rolled out significantly tougher fitness parameters after a bruising summer exposed systemic gaps in player conditioning, according to reports in The Times of India and Sporting News.

The Bronco Test — a 1,200-metre shuttle run across five sets of 20m, 40m, and 60m sprints — now carries a cutoff of 5 minutes and 15 to 20 seconds, down from the previous six-minute benchmark. Immediately after completing it, players must finish a 2-kilometre run within 9 to 10 minutes. Previously, the 2K run was a standalone test with tighter time limits — 8 minutes 15 seconds for fast bowlers, 8 minutes 30 seconds for others — but conducting both tests back-to-back makes the combined threshold considerably more demanding.

The YoYo test benchmark remains at 16.5, though the BCCI views it as supplementary rather than the primary fitness marker going forward.

The Injury Crisis That Forced the Rethink

India's 2026 white-ball tours were battered by injuries. The team was without pace-bowling all-rounders Hardik Pandya and Nitish Kumar Reddy for the entire Ireland and England legs. Varun Chakaravarthy, Harshit Rana, Jasprit Bumrah, and Washington Sundar all broke down at various points, forcing them to miss matches.

The results were devastating: a 0-2 T20I whitewash in Ireland, a 0-4 T20I series loss in England, and a 1-2 ODI series defeat. Only a subsequent 3-0 T20I clean sweep over Zimbabwe salvaged some pride.

"The Indian team management flagged that he was overweight by four kgs. The CoE should have been much more vigilant. He was 97 kgs when he was cleared to be picked for the Indian team for the UK tour."

— BCCI source, via The Times of India

Customized Targets Under Scrutiny

A BCCI source told The Times of India that the CoE had been setting different baseline parameters for individual players, a practice that effectively lowered the bar for some senior cricketers. The source said certain senior players were given "much more comfortable targets" to clear fitness tests.

The case of Harshit Rana became a flashpoint. The fast bowler suffered a right knee ligament injury in February that ruled him out of the T20 World Cup and the IPL. He was fast-tracked back into the squad for the UK tour without competitive match preparation — and was reportedly 97 kg, four kilograms over his target weight. He subsequently suffered a Grade 1 hamstring strain during the T20I series against England.

The CoE has since capped Rana's weight limit at 96 kg, and he is currently at 94 kg.

Pre-Season Testing Underway

India's top centrally-contracted cricketers reported to the CoE on Saturday for mandatory pre-season fitness evaluations, less than 48 hours after completing a two-Test away series against Sri Lanka, according to Yardbarker.

Senior all-rounder Ravindra Jadeja, keeper-batter Rishabh Pant, opener Yashasvi Jaiswal, and T20I captain Shreyas Iyer underwent the rigorous drills alongside Rinku Singh, Sanju Samson, and Ruturaj Gaikwad.

Fast bowlers Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna were exempted due to heavy workloads from the Sri Lanka Tests. Jasprit Bumrah, Hardik Pandya, and Nitish Kumar Reddy will undergo testing only after being declared fully fit from their ongoing rehabilitation.

A Packed Home Season Looms

The fitness overhaul arrives ahead of a demanding home season. The BCCI's annual "India Cricket" calendar commences in September with three T20Is against Afghanistan in New Delhi, followed by the Asian Games in Japan and a home series against the West Indies.

Sports scientist Wayne Lombard, speaking to MyKhel, cautioned that the Bronco Test alone is not a silver bullet. "Its real value comes when the data is used to build better, individualised training programmes," he said, suggesting the test is a useful tool but should be embedded in a broader fitness culture rather than treated as a one-off benchmark.

What to Watch

The real test of the BCCI's fitness overhaul will come across the gruelling eight-month home season stretching through to the 2027 IPL. Whether tighter benchmarks translate into fewer breakdowns — or simply push players into overtraining — remains to be seen. For now, the board has drawn a clear line: the days of relaxed fitness standards are over.
